notes: The her of let her not go answers to no object morpheme on that verb and is added under rule 44's supplied-object clause, exactly as the it of he let it fall is; the competing reading folding it into musar as a resumption under rule 25 is named in the unit note, and rule 44's clause is the more specific ruling.
The her of Keep her is the object suffix on that verb (rule 18).

The article assimilated into the pointed ba- is a real token and goes unrepresented, since the ASV writes instruction with no the (rule 12); the be- itself takes the of the English verb reaches its object through, a present preposition taking the word before rule 44's supplied reading.
